The Ford Escape family

4 generations and variants in the Index, 2001–2026. Oldest first; every card opens the full page, with its own versions, figures and story.

  1. 2001–2007

    Ford Escape (first generation)

    Ford and Mazda built America's compact-SUV template — and then, in 2005, put the first hybrid SUV on the US market wearing an Escape badge.

    200 hp8.9 sec 0-60105 mph top1,191,511 built
    3.0 Duratec V6 · 2.0 Zetec (2001–04) · Escape Hybrid (2005–07)
  2. 2008–2012

    Ford Escape (second generation)

    Same bones, squarer suit: the 2008–12 Escape rode the gas-price panic to a quarter-million sales a year while its hybrid twin racked up taxi miles by the hundreds of thousands.

    171 hp9.5 sec 0-60105 mph top1,035,915 built
    2.5 Duratec (2009–12) · 3.0 V6, 240 hp · Escape Hybrid (2008–12)
  3. 2013–2019

    Ford Escape (third generation)

    One Ford made the Escape and Europe's Kuga the same car — and America bought more than 300,000 a year, 4 years running. Over 2 million sold makes this the biggest Escape of all.

    237 hp7.0 sec 0-60120 mph top2,037,678 built
    2.0 EcoBoost · 1.6 EcoBoost (2013–16) · 2.5 Duratec (base) · 1.5 EcoBoost (2017–19)
  4. 2020–2026

    Ford Escape (fourth generation)

    Car-like on purpose, hybrid again at last, and retired after 2026: the last Escape is the quickest (5.7 to 60) and the most efficient (101 MPGe) the nameplate ever got.

    250 hp5.7 sec 0-60125 mph top888,495 built
    2.0 EcoBoost, 250 hp · 1.5 EcoBoost, 181 hp · Hybrid, 200 hp · Plug-In Hybrid, 209 hp
